MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of January 1, 2024 ("Effective Date") by and between Enterprise Corporation, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 1000 Enterprise Way, San Francisco, CA 94105 ("Enterprise") and the entity identified in the applicable Order Form ("Customer").

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with the subject entity. "Control," for purposes of this definition, means direct or indirect ownership or control of more than 50% of the voting interests of the subject entity.

1.2 "Confidential Information" means any information, technical data, or know-how, including, but not limited to, that which relates to research, product plans, products, services, customers, markets, software, developments, inventions, processes, designs, drawings, engineering, hardware configuration information, marketing, or finances of the disclosing party.

1.3 "Data Protection Laws" means all laws and regulations, including laws and regulations of the European Union, the European Economic Area and their member states, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States, that apply to the Processing of Personal Data, including, where applicable, EU Data Protection Laws.

1.4 "EU Data Protection Laws" means (i) Regulation 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (General Data Protection Regulation or "GDPR"); (ii) Directive 2002/58/EC concerning the processing of personal data and the protection of privacy in the electronic communications sector; and (iii) national legislation implementing or supplementing (i) or (ii).

1.5 "Personal Data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person to the extent such information is processed as personal data under applicable Data Protection Laws in connection with the Services.

1.6 "Processing" means any operation or set of operations which is performed upon Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organization, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, blocking, erasure, or destruction.

1.7 "Security Incident" means any unauthorized or unlawful Processing of Personal Data or any accidental loss, destruction, damage, theft, unauthorized disclosure, or access to Personal Data Processed by Enterprise.

1.8 "Services" means the software-as-a-service products and related services ordered by Customer and provided by Enterprise pursuant to an Order Form.

1.9 "Sub-processor" means any third party engaged by Enterprise or by any other Sub-processor to Process Personal Data on behalf of Customer.

1.10 "Technical and Organizational Measures" means the security measures applied by Enterprise to protect Personal Data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure, or access.

2. SERVICES

2.1 Provision of Services. Enterprise shall make the Services available to Customer pursuant to this Agreement and the applicable Order Form. Customer's use of the Services is subject to this Agreement and any additional terms and conditions that may apply to specific features or functionality.

2.2 Service Level. Enterprise shall provide the Services in accordance with the service level agreement attached as Exhibit A. Enterprise reserves the right to modify the service level agreement upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer.

2.3 Changes to Services. Enterprise may make changes to the Services from time to time, provided that such changes do not materially decrease the overall functionality of the Services. Enterprise shall provide Customer with notice of any material changes.

3. DATA PROTECTION

3.1 Data Processing. Enterprise shall Process Personal Data only in accordance with Customer's documented instructions and for the purposes set forth in the Data Processing Addendum attached as Exhibit B. Enterprise shall not Process Personal Data for any other purpose without Customer's prior written consent.

3.2 Confidentiality. Enterprise shall ensure that all personnel authorized to Process Personal Data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.

3.3 Security Measures. Enterprise shall implement and maintain appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures to protect Personal Data against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, theft, alteration, or disclosure.

3.4 Sub-processors. Customer hereby provides general authorization for Enterprise to engage Sub-processors to Process Personal Data on Customer's behalf. Enterprise shall maintain an up-to-date list of Sub-processors and shall notify Customer of any intended changes to such list by updating the list at [website]. Customer may object to such changes in writing within fifteen (15) days of the notification.

3.5 Security Incidents. In the event of a Security Incident, Enterprise shall notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of the Security Incident. Enterprise shall provide Customer with a description of the Security Incident, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and Personal Data records concerned, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address the Security Incident.

3.6 Data Subject Requests. Enterprise shall assist Customer in responding to requests from data subjects exercising their rights under applicable Data Protection Laws, to the extent legally permitted.

3.7 Data Protection Impact Assessments. Enterprise shall assist Customer in ensuring compliance with obligations relating to data protection impact assessments and prior consultation with supervisory authorities, to the extent required under applicable Data Protection Laws.

3.8 International Data Transfers. Enterprise shall not transfer Personal Data outside of the European Economic Area unless appropriate safeguards are in place in accordance with applicable Data Protection Laws, including but not limited to Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission.

3.9 Data Return and Deletion. Upon termination of the Services, Enterprise shall, at Customer's choice, return or delete all Personal Data and delete existing copies, unless applicable law requires storage of the Personal Data.

3.10 Audit Rights. Enterprise shall make available to Customer all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Agreement and Data Protection Laws and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, by Customer or a third-party auditor mandated by Customer.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY

4.1 Obligations. Each party agrees to maintain the confidentiality of the other party's Confidential Information and shall not disclose such Confidential Information to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees to use the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information, but in no event less than reasonable care.

4.2 Exceptions. The obligations of confidentiality shall not apply to information that: (a) is or becomes publicly known through no fault of the receiving party; (b) was rightfully known to the receiving party prior to disclosure by the disclosing party; (c) is rightfully received from a third party without any obligation of confidentiality; or (d) is independently developed by the receiving party without use of the disclosing party's Confidential Information.

4.3 Compelled Disclosure. If the receiving party is required by law to disclose the disclosing party's Confidential Information, the receiving party shall provide the disclosing party with prompt written notice of such requirement, to the extent legally permitted, so that the disclosing party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy.

5. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

5.1 Ownership. Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data. Enterprise retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Services, including all software, technology, and intellectual property rights therein.

5.2 Feedback. If Customer provides any suggestions, comments, or other feedback to Enterprise regarding the Services, Enterprise may use such feedback without restriction or obligation to Customer.

5.3 License. Enterprise grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to use the Services solely for Customer's internal business purposes during the term of this Agreement.

6. WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMERS

6.1 Warranties. Each party represents and warrants that it has the legal power and authority to enter into this Agreement. Enterprise represents and warrants that the Services will perform substantially in accordance with the documentation and will not introduce any material malicious code into Customer's systems.

6.2 Disclaimer. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTIES, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, OR STATUTORY, INCLUDING ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, OR NON-INFRINGEMENT. ENTERPRISE DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE SERVICES WILL BE UNINTERRUPTED OR ERROR-FREE.

7. INDEMNIFICATION

7.1 Indemnification by Enterprise. Enterprise shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer from and against any claims, damages, losses, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from any third-party claim that the Services infringe any patent, copyright, trademark, or trade secret of such third party.

7.2 Indemnification by Customer. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Enterprise from and against any claims, damages, losses, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from any third-party claim relating to Customer Data or Customer's use of the Services in violation of this Agreement.

7.3 Procedure. The indemnifying party shall control the defense of any indemnified claim, provided that the indemnifying party may not settle any claim that imposes any obligation on the indemnified party without the indemnified party's prior written consent.

8. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

8.1 Limitation. IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS, DATA, OR BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF ACTION OR THE THEORY OF LIABILITY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

8.2 Cap. EACH PARTY'S TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL FEES PAID BY CUSTOMER TO ENTERPRISE DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE CLAIM.

9. TERM AND TERMINATION

9.1 Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue until terminated by either party in accordance with this Section 9.

9.2 Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party.

9.3 Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice thereof.

9.4 Effect of Termination. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement: (a) all licenses granted hereunder shall immediately terminate; (b) Customer shall pay all outstanding fees due to Enterprise; (c) Enterprise shall return or delete Customer Data as set forth in Section 3.9; and (d) Sections 4, 6, 7, and 8 shall survive termination.

10. GENERAL PROVISIONS

10.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

10.2 Dispute Resolution. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party hereby consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts.

10.3 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party, except that Enterprise may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.

10.4 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with all Order Forms and Exhibits, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous agreements, representations, and understandings, whether written or oral.

10.5 Amendment. This Agreement may only be amended by a written instrument signed by both parties.

10.6 Waiver. The failure of either party to enforce any provision of this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of such provision or the right to enforce it at a later time.

10.7 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

10.8 Force Majeure. Neither party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform due to causes beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to acts of God, war, terrorism, pandemic, natural disaster, or internet service provider failure.

10.9 Notices. All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed delivered upon: (a) personal delivery; (b) the second business day after mailing by registered or certified mail; or (c) the first business day after sending by email with confirmation of receipt.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

EXHIBIT A - SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT

1. UPTIME COMMITMENT

Enterprise commits to maintaining 99.9% uptime for the Services during each calendar month ("Uptime Commitment"). Uptime is calculated based on the total minutes in the month minus the total minutes of unplanned downtime.

2. EXCLUSIONS

The Uptime Commitment does not apply to downtime resulting from: (a) scheduled maintenance performed during the maintenance window of 2:00 AM - 4:00 AM Pacific Time on Sundays; (b) issues caused by Customer's equipment, software, or internet connectivity; (c) force majeure events; or (d) Customer's use of the Services in violation of this Agreement.

3. SERVICE CREDITS

If Enterprise fails to meet the Uptime Commitment, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit as follows:
- 99.0% to 99.8% uptime: 5% of monthly fees
- 98.0% to 98.9% uptime: 10% of monthly fees
- Below 98.0% uptime: 25% of monthly fees

Service credits shall be Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any downtime. Customer must request service credits within thirty (30) days of the end of the applicable month.

EXHIBIT B - DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM

This Data Processing Addendum ("DPA") forms part of the Master Services Agreement and reflects the parties' agreement on the Processing of Personal Data.

1. SCOPE

This DPA applies to the Processing of Personal Data by Enterprise on behalf of Customer in connection with the Services.

2. ROLES

Customer is the controller of Personal Data. Enterprise is the processor of Personal Data on behalf of Customer.

3. DETAILS OF PROCESSING

3.1 Categories of Data Subjects: Customer's employees, contractors, and end users.

3.2 Categories of Personal Data: Name, email address, job title, company name, and usage data.

3.3 Purposes of Processing: Provision of the Services, customer support, and improvement of the Services.

3.4 Duration of Processing: Throughout the term of the Agreement, unless earlier deleted.

4. OBLIGATIONS

Enterprise shall: (a) Process Personal Data only in accordance with Customer's documented instructions; (b) ensure that personnel authorized to Process Personal Data are bound by confidentiality obligations; (c) implement appropriate security measures; (d) not engage Sub-processors without prior written authorization; (e) assist Customer in responding to data subject requests; (f) notify Customer of any Security Incident; (g) assist Customer with data protection impact assessments; and (h) return or delete Personal Data upon termination.

5. STANDARD CONTRACTUAL CLAUSES

For transfers of Personal Data from the European Economic Area to a country not providing adequate protection, the parties agree to comply with the Standard Contractual Clauses (Processors) approved by the European Commission, as applicable.

[END OF AGREEMENT]
